autor: Bartošek of Drahonice, a squire in the service of King Sigismund
quelle: Kronika Bartoška z Drahonic, ed. Jaroslav Goll, in Fontes rerum Bohemicarum V (Prague 1893), pp. 589–628; passages from pp. 592 and 613–615. Page images: Czech Academy of Sciences, 'Czech medieval sources FONTES' (book 1103). English: the site's working translation.
hinweis: Bartošek of Drahonice was a Catholic squire of the royal party: in 1421 he rode out with the king's garrison when Prague Castle surrendered ('equitavimus', we rode), and at Lipany his own servant fought with the Karlštejn garrison on the lords' side. His Latin chronicle of 1419–1443 is short-sentenced and annalistic, and the fullest near-contemporary account of Lipany. The edition prints it in two columns; the passages were read from the page images. Omissions are marked [...]; the editor's supplements in round brackets are kept, and his corrections of the manuscript are named in the notes.

sections.blurb: Žižka's brotherhood defeats the army of Prague near Malešov: Hussites against Hussites, fourteen hundred dead on both sides.

units.orig: Anno domini MCCCCXXIV Zizka cum suis et Johanne Bzdinka et complicibus Pragenses mediante conflictu vicit et ipsis multos currus cum pixidibus recepit; CCC et (ultra) hospites Pragenses interfecti; et factum est feria V ante Viti in illa sillaba Jul pri mi prope fortalicium Malessow retro Montes Cuthnas; et dicebatur a veridicis, quod ex utraque parte MCCCC sunt ibi in loco interfecti, inter quos ex parte Pragensium interfecti sunt strenui milites Turkowecz tenens Pragense vexillum in manibus, dominus Hlas, Wykerz iuvenis, Hlawacz de Destnycz et CCCXXVI hospites Pragenses preter advenas et mechanicos Pragenses.
units.en: In the year of the Lord 1424 Žižka with his men, with John Bzdinka and their companions, defeated the Praguers in battle and took many of their wagons with their guns; three hundred and more householders of Prague were killed. It happened on the Thursday before St Vitus, at the syllable 'Jul pri mi', near the fort of Malešov beyond Kutná Hora; and it was said by truthful men that fourteen hundred were killed there on the spot on both sides, among them, on the Prague side, the brave knights Turkovec, who held the Prague banner in his hands, lord Hlas, the young Vikéř, Hlaváč of Deštnice, and three hundred and twenty-six householders of Prague, besides foreigners and the craftsmen of Prague.
units.note: Hussites against Hussites: Žižka's brotherhood against the army of Prague, the game's 'Malešov' choice. 'Hospites' are the Prague householders, as against foreigners and craftsmen. The 'syllable' refers to the Cisiojanus, a mnemonic verse calendar; the editor notes that the battle was fought on Wednesday 7 June and that the syllable for that day is 'Jun', not 'Jul'. 'Ultra' is supplied by Dobner. John Bzdinka is the Prague captain whose rule against desertion Toman compares with the ordinance's article 10.

sections.blurb: The lords' league, Utraquist and Catholic, against the Taborites and Orphans: the two armies, the feigned flight, the brethren leaving their wagons, the death of both Prokops, the count, and the submission at Kolín.

units.orig: Conflictum magnum. Eodem anno videlicet MCCCCXXXIV dominico, die solis, ipso die sancti Crispini, in illa sillaba cris pan, die XXX mensis Maii hora vesperarum vel quasi, [...] inter civitates Kurzym et Brodam Boemicalem prope villam. Et ipso die sol erat in signo Geminorum et luna in gauda sive fine Piscium.
units.en: The great battle. In the same year, namely 1434, on Sunday, the day of the sun, on the very day of St Crispin, at the syllable 'cris pan', on the thirtieth day of the month of May, at about the hour of vespers, [...] between the towns of Kouřim and Český Brod, near the village. And on that day the sun was in the sign of Gemini and the moon at the tail or end of Pisces.
units.note: The omitted lines date the day by indiction, the Sunday letter, and the years of Pope Eugene IV and of Sigismund as emperor. The name of the village is missing in the manuscript; Pešina supplied Hřiby. The editor notes that St Crispin's day would be 25 October; the chronicler has mixed up his calendar. Bartošek dates the battle like an astrologer: a knight of the royal party writing of the day the Hussite field armies ended.

units.orig: Nobiles barones et domini dominus Menhardus de Nova domo, dominus Ptaczko de Lipii alias de Ratay et de Polna, dominus Alsso de Sternberk alias de Holicz, [...] predicti domini barones et milites et cives et clientes habentes omnes simul, ut communiter dicebatur, mille equites et decem milia peditum vel citra et duodecim vel citra sexagenas curruum cum defendiculis ipsorum et pixidibus;
units.en: The noble barons and lords, lord Menhart of Jindřichův Hradec, lord Ptáček of Lipí, also called of Rataje and of Polná, lord Aleš of Šternberk, also called of Holice, [...] the said lords, barons and knights and citizens and squires, having all together, as was commonly said, a thousand horse and ten thousand foot or fewer, and twelve threescore wagons or fewer, with their shields and guns;
units.note: The omitted list names some forty lords, knights and contingents: Utraquist and Catholic lords together, the men of Ulrich of Rožmberk, the Plzeň district, the garrison of Karlštejn, citizens of the Prague towns and of Mělník. Among them is a young lord of Kunštát 'residing at Poděbrady', whom the editor identifies as George of Poděbrady, the later king; and 'Leonard, servant of Bartošek of Drahonice', the chronicler's own man. The lords fought with wagons too: twelve threescore, seven hundred and twenty.

units.orig: et presbiter Procopius Rasus, tunc capitaneus secte Taborensium, cum ipsis Taborensibus campestribus, et Johannes dictus Czapko de Ssan, tunc supremus capitaneus secte Zizkonis Orfanorum similiter in campis a XII annis continuancium et bellancium, et presbiter Prokopko dictus Parvus Procopius et Andreas dictus Kersky, capitaneus eciam Taborensium de Thabor, civibus de ibidem et civibus de Werona, Slana, Zacz, Luna, Kurzim, Kolin, Montis Cutnis, Broda Boemicalis, Czaslaw, Nymburg, Grecz regine, Jaromirz, Trutnow, Dwuor, Altamuta, Glatovia, Prachaticz, Domazlicz, Piesek, Litomierzicz, Rohacz de Duba, Zagimacz de Giwissovicz cum aliis ipsorum complicibus, ut communiter dicebatur, VIIC equites et novem milia vel citra (peditum) .... curruum, XL et plus pixides dictas hufnicze cum aliis pixidibus et ipsorum defendiculis parte ex altera conflictum intraverunt.
units.en: and the priest Prokop the Bald, then captain of the Taborite sect, with the Taborites of the field, and John called Čapek of Sány, then supreme captain of the sect of Žižka, the Orphans, who had likewise continued and fought in the field for twelve years, and the priest Prokůpek called Prokop the Lesser, and Andrew called Keřský, also a captain of the Taborites of Tábor, with the citizens of that place and the citizens of Beroun, Slaný, Žatec, Louny, Kouřim, Kolín, Kutná Hora, Český Brod, Čáslav, Nymburk, Hradec Králové, Jaroměř, Trutnov, Dvůr, Vysoké Mýto, Klatovy, Prachatice, Domažlice, Písek, Litoměřice, Roháč of Dubá, Sezima of Jevišovice, with their other companions, as was commonly said, seven hundred horse and nine thousand foot or fewer, .... wagons, forty and more guns called 'houfnice' with other guns and their shields, entered the battle on the other side.
units.note: 'In the field for twelve years': the field armies as a standing army of brotherhoods and towns. Roháč of Dubá is John Roháč, who had set his name second after Žižka's under the ordinance of 1423 (Ordinance Preamble [1]). The number of wagons is missing in the manuscript; Toman supplied six threescore from the Old Czech Annals. 'Peditum' is supplied by Pešina. 'Hufnice', the howitzer, is one of the Czech words the war gave to other languages.

units.orig: Et predicti barones domini fingentes se quasi ab ipsis fugere et a gauda curruum ipsorum optimas gentes domini Ulrici de Roznberg predicti, de districtibus Plznensi, Prachinensi, domini Menhardi et de Carlstain in gauda et tergo curruum ipsorum cum vexillo domini de Roznberk clam et secrete, quod hastas et balistas apprehensas ad terram declinantes, ordinaverunt et verso quasi tergo et gauda curruum ipsorum ab ipsis hostibus Taborensibus et Orfanis oc quasi recedere et fugere conantes. Tandem ipsi hostes ipsos cum curribus suis ad gaudam curruum dominorum insequebantur de pixidibus acriter sagittantes et clamantes: fugiunt, fugiunt et fugam dant! et appropinquati ad currus dominorum cum ipsorum curribus quasi per medium stadium vel citra de curribus ipsorum hostiliter exiverunt in currus dominorum irruere volentes.
units.en: And the said barons and lords, feigning to flee from them, placed the best men of the said lord Ulrich of Rožmberk, of the districts of Plzeň and Prácheň, of lord Menhart and of Karlštejn, at the tail and rear of their wagons with the lord of Rožmberk's banner, secretly and hidden, holding their lances and crossbows lowered to the ground; and turning, as it were, their backs and the tail of their wagons, they made as if to withdraw and flee from those enemies, the Taborites and Orphans. At last the enemy pursued them with their wagons to the tail of the lords' wagons, shooting fiercely from their guns and shouting: 'They flee, they flee, they are taking flight!' And having come up with their wagons to within about half a furlong of the lords' wagons, they went out of their wagons in force, meaning to rush the lords' wagons.
units.note: The article of the ordinance broken here is the fifth: no troop shall break away from its order (Ordinance [5]). The manuscript reads 'surgentes', rising; 'fingentes', feigning, is the editor's correction, which the sense requires. The shout is the same as at Vyšehrad in 1420, 'fugiunt, fugiunt!' (Laurence Vyšehrad [3]), which then won the day.

units.orig: Tandem gentes dominorum et domini erecto velo sive vexillo domini Roznberk et alio extra suos currus contra ipsos iam prope existentes exierunt et viriliter cum ipsis pugnaverunt et ipsos sic audacter et acriter percusserunt, quod sicut diceret Miserere mei deus, illum psalmum, Taborenses et Orfani fugam et tergum dederunt et in suos currus reverti volebant, ut ipsos circum se clauderent, sicque predicti domini et gentes cum ipsis ita celeriter et agiliter ipsos percucientes insequebantur, quod cum ipsis in eorum currus incurrerunt et ibi in eisdem curribus dictos presbiteros ambos Procopios predictos et plures presbiteros de eorum secta maligna interfecerunt et ipsorum multos in curribus et de curribus fugientes et ipsos insequentes, pedestres et equestres, interfecerunt et occiderunt et Gyram Ussati et Marssonem Krsnak subcapitaneos captivaverunt.
units.en: At last the lords' men and the lords, raising the standard or banner of the lord of Rožmberk and another, went out of their wagons against them, who were now close, fought manfully with them, and struck them so boldly and fiercely that, in the time one might say the psalm 'Miserere mei deus', the Taborites and Orphans turned their backs in flight and tried to get back into their wagons to close them round themselves; and the said lords and their men pursued them, striking them so quickly and nimbly that they ran into their wagons together with them, and there in those same wagons they killed both the said priests named Prokop and many priests of their wicked sect, and killed and slew many of them in the wagons and fleeing from the wagons, pursuing them on foot and on horse, and took the under-captains Jíra Ušatý and Mareš Kršňák prisoner.
units.note: The wagon fort could not be closed again once its men had left it: the lords came in with them. 'In the time one might say the Miserere' is explained by a later hand in one manuscript as the time it takes to recite that psalm. Both Prokops, the Great and the Lesser, fell.

units.titel: The count, and the flight to Kolín
units.orig: Et sic communiter dicebatur (ab hiis), qui ibidem tunc erant, quia predicte secte decem milia cum 2½C habuerunt, et soli hoc idem dicebant, et vix eorum IIIC fugierunt; hos omnes in loco et incursu versus Brodam Boemicalem et prope Brodam interfecerunt et cremaverunt et omnes currus, pixides, arma et defendicula ipsis receperunt; dictus vero Czapko et Andreas Kersky, capitanei predicti, in Coloniam fugierunt equites cum eorum paucis complicibus peditibus.
units.en: And so it was commonly said by those who were there at the time that the said sects had ten thousand two hundred and fifty, and they themselves said the same, and scarcely three hundred of them escaped; all these they killed and burned on the spot and in the pursuit towards Český Brod and near Brod, and took from them all their wagons, guns, arms and shields; but the said Čapek and Andrew Keřský, the captains, fled to Kolín, the horsemen, with a few of their men on foot.
units.note: The sentence is unclear: 'scarcely three hundred escaped' and then 'all these they killed'. 'Hos' is the editor's correction of the manuscript's 'hoc'; the sense seems to be that of the rest scarcely three hundred got away. Čapek, the Orphans' supreme captain, rode off with the horse while the foot died: the cavalry left the infantry, as Toman judged (p. 390).

units.orig: Et domini et gentes suprascripti ipsos in crastino usque Coloniam sunt insecuti et ibidem quadam concordia interveniente, videlicet ut idem Czapko et Kersky et Colonienses cum ipsis adherentibus sint Prage in termino seu concursu magno omnium dominorum, civitatum et terrigenarum et, qui(d)cunque ibi in festo sancti Johannis Baptiste dictatum et conclusum fuerit per dominos terrigenas et civitates, in illis debent stare et contentari, et sic predicti domini et terrigene campum distraxerunt et ad domicilia redierunt proclamato termino Prage in festo sancti Johannis Baptiste.
units.en: And the lords and men named above pursued them the next day as far as Kolín, and there an agreement was made: that Čapek and Keřský and the men of Kolín with those who held with them should be in Prague at the session or great assembly of all the lords, towns and men of the land, and should stand by and be content with whatever was decided and concluded there on the feast of St John the Baptist by the lords of the land and the towns; and so the said lords and men of the land broke camp and went home, an assembly having been proclaimed at Prague for the feast of St John the Baptist.
units.note: The field armies' end is not a massacre but a submission to the estates: the brotherhood's captains bind themselves to what the lords and towns decide. Two years later the estates accepted the Compacts and Sigismund as king.
